stem: An older adult has declining vision and slower reaction time and asks whether age alone means driving must stop immediately. Which nursing approach is most appropriate?

options.A: Recommend driving cessation solely because of chronological age without first assessing vision, cognition, motor function, or driving-related abilities.
options.B: Assess driving-related vision, cognition, and motor/sensory function and discuss referral for a formal driving evaluation when specific concerns are identified.
options.C: Ignore declining vision or slower reaction time because healthcare professionals have no role in counseling about driving-safety concerns.
options.D: Treat one abnormal office measure as conclusive proof of unsafe driving without considering the broader functional assessment.

rationale: NHTSA states that decisions about driving ability should never be based on age alone. Its clinician guidance describes assessment of driving-related functional domains including vision, cognition, and motor/sensory function to identify specific concerns and supports referral for additional driving evaluation when indicated. B is correct.
educational_objective: Evaluate older-driver safety using individualized functional assessment rather than chronological age alone and refer for further driving evaluation when specific concerns are identified.
source_document_title: Older Drivers; Licensing Agency Referrals / Clinician’s Guide to Assessing and Counseling Older Drivers
source_version_date: Current NHTSA older-driver guidance; live-rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: Older Drivers: decisions about ability to drive should never be based on age alone; changes in vision, physical fitness, reflexes/attention can affect safety. Licensing Agency Referrals: CADReS assesses key functional areas of vision, cognition, and motor/sensory functions and helps identify concerns related to driving; clinicians may refer drivers for additional evaluation.
source_claim_supported: Older-driver fitness should be assessed individually rather than determined by age alone; vision, cognition and motor/sensory function are relevant domains, and further driving evaluation may be appropriate when concerns are identified.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance, printed p.9: perform targeted screening assessments; educate adults age 65 and older; assess health risks and home/environmental management needs.
blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — older-adult driving-safety assessment and counseling

correction_summary: Retained key B, corroborated the clinician-referral page with NHTSA's current statement that driving ability should never be based on age alone, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium.

audit_findings.source_authority: NHTSA current older-driver/clinician guidance; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.exact_locator: NHTSA Older Drivers age-alone statement and Licensing Agency Referrals CADReS description; NCSBN Health Promotion p.9 screenshot verified
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item appropriately uses individualized functional domains and referral, without allowing age alone or one office measure to establish driving unfitness.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because NHTSA explicitly states driving ability should not be decided by age alone.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because clinicians have a recognized role in assessing/counseling and referral for driving-safety concerns.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because one abnormal office measure is not treated as conclusive proof of driving performance in isolation.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B uses the recommended individualized assessment/referral approach.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives are counseling/assessment approaches for the same older driver.
audit_findings.blueprint: Health Promotion and Maintenance — age/risk-appropriate assessment and safety education.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read current NHTSA Older Drivers and referral/CADReS material plus NCSBN p.9, then all options, rationale and age-alone caveat. B remained uniquely correct.
